706:478.description:
A small pill carrying a count, a status or a short label.

An icon leads the label or stands alone; it never trails, and a badge is never a control. Something that opens a menu or acts is a `Button` beside the badge.

The label carries the colour over a tint of it, so the pill stays near white.

variant:
- fillGray: The default, and what most badges should be: a count or a neutral label with no verdict.
- lightGray: `fillGray`'s quieter twin, for the same counts and labels where the solid one is too loud.
- safe: Something that came off or is fine, chosen by meaning rather than weight.
- warn: Something waiting on the user or at risk, chosen by meaning rather than weight.
- danger: Something that failed, chosen by meaning rather than weight.
- purple: Work that has landed, and what an agent wrote: merged and integrated are purple.
- blue: Something calm and informational, a note rather than a verdict. Not for merged.
- pop: The accent, and the rarest colour in the app: at most one per surface.

In Figma: The drawing shows the light theme's tint in both themes: on a dark ground the code tints from the variant's fill instead, and Figma can't change a layer's opacity by mode.

2763:6859.description:
A condition that holds right now, set into the layout above the thing it affects: live updates paused, a machine offline, a server that won't answer. It stays while the condition is true and leaves when it clears, so it has no close button; the caller renders it only while it applies.

The title says the condition; `children` is an optional second sentence under it. A quiet note set inside a card, such as why a chart is empty, leaves the title out and is that one sentence in the description's type. The icon and the action line up with the first line. The action is the fix (Retry, Reconnect, Pull): one small ghost `Button`, which takes the banner's colour.

Use a Snackbar for the outcome of something the user just did; a banner is for state.

variant:
- warn: Something is degraded but still usable: what the user sees may be stale.
- danger: Something failed, and the surface can't do its job until it is fixed.
- pop: Something new the user can act on. The accent, so at most one per surface.
- safe: A condition worth confirming in place. Rarely needed: most good news is a Snackbar.
- gray: A neutral note with no verdict.

In Figma: Turn on Description for the second sentence.

Rules: https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/master/packages/but-ui/design/components/banners.md

217:317.description:
The button: Base UI's, so `focusableWhenDisabled` and `render` work, styled by variant and size. An icon goes in as a child, before or after the label, and so does a `Kbd variant="button"`; an icon-only button takes `iconOnly` and needs an `aria-label`. It is `type="button"` unless told otherwise, so one inside a form doesn't submit it by accident.

To make another component look like a button — a toolbar item, a number field's stepper — give it `getButtonClassName` instead; to make a Base UI trigger one, pass this as its `render`.

variant:
- pop: The accent, solid, as a checked checkbox or switch is: the primary action of the whole surface. At most one per surface: if two things pop, neither does.
- gray: Solid gray ground. Lifts a button above the ones around it without spending color — a highlight, not a primary action.
- outline: The default. A ghost with an edge, for a button on open ground where nothing else marks it as a target. Ranks equally with `ghost`: mixing the two in one group separates kinds of control (the PR toolbar outlines its Auto-merge toggle among ghost actions), never levels of importance.
- outline-inverted: `outline` for a button on an inverted ground — a selected row, not dark mode.
- danger: For an act the user cannot take back: deleting, discarding, hard-resetting. Chosen by consequence, so it sits outside the ladder.
- danger-solid: `danger` at full strength, for the answer to a confirmation that destroys something.
- ghost: No ground, no border. For actions inside something already a container: a row, a toolbar, a popup.
- ghost-inverted: `ghost` for a button on an inverted ground — a selected row, not dark mode.

In Figma: `state` is the drawing's only: hover is the button under the pointer, which the code draws from CSS rather than a prop.

Rules: https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/master/packages/but-ui/design/components/buttons.md, https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/master/packages/but-ui/design/foundations/emphasis.md

3006:44182.description:
One part of a meta line, as 🍑 But UI's MetaPart draws it: a glyph, then the words, in a header's meta line or a row's where MetaCount has no type for what the part says, such as "2 PRs · 1 failing", "CLI 0.2.1662 outdated" or "Needs force push". Amber is work waiting on you, blue is work to send, green is an agent at work or a state that is fine, red is something that failed; neutral is the rest.

A part that opens what it describes takes `href`, and only then is it underlined, dotted, in its own colour; a part that only explains on hover is a plain part in a `Tooltip`. Wrap the words a narrow pane can do without in MetaWord, so "2 PRs · 1 failing" reads "2 · 1" there.

In Figma: `type` picks one of the parts the meta lines note describes, with its glyph, colour and words; several wrap a MetaCount. `width=narrow` is a pane under 640px. There is no pull request part: a branch with one is ViewHeader's `view=branch-pr`. `agent-working` and `agent-waiting` are but.dev's AgentsPart around a MetaCount.

Rules: https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/master/packages/but-ui/design/components/meta-lines.md

2210:1708.description:
One line of consequence, floated over the surface that caused it: a glyph, a sentence, and at most one button, fenced off behind a divider: Undo when what just happened can be taken back, or a close button when the snackbar waits to be dismissed by hand. Never both: an undoable snackbar leaves on its own, so it has nothing to close. A whole Toasts card would state a title and a description; a snackbar has only the sentence, so it can sit close to the thing it is about rather than in the corner of the window.

Every variant wears the same surface: the verdict is carried by the glyph alone, so a run of snackbars reads as one row of statements rather than a traffic light.

variant:
- info: Something happened worth saying, with no verdict attached.
- warning: An act that came off with a catch: it ran, but not quite as asked.
- danger: An act that failed, or refused to run.
- safe: An act that came off.

In Figma: `action` is `undo` when the code is given `onUndo`, `dismiss` when it's given `onDismiss`.

Rules: https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/master/packages/but-ui/design/patterns/toasts-and-snackbars.md

2805:61892.description:
Where toasts appear. Render it once inside Base UI's `Toast.Provider`; anything under the provider raises one through `Toast.useToastManager().add({ type, title, description, actionProps })`.

Each toast is a card in the window's bottom-right corner: a glyph, a title naming what happened, a description that can hold real content, at most one action under it, and a close button. Every type wears the same surface; the glyph alone carries the verdict.

In Figma: `type` is the `type` a toast is added with: one of each, drawn.

Rules: https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/master/packages/but-ui/design/patterns/toasts-and-snackbars.md
